source_reference: Tohoku, Chapter IV, Section 4.3, printed p. 193

existing_source_repair.mathematical_effect: The quotient spectral-sequence initial term uses Tor over the original ring, written in the formalization as Tor_a^R(S,M), rather than the diplomatic erroneous quotient-ring superscript.

checks: For left modules, S=R/I is used as an (S,R)-bimodule and Tor_a^R(S,M) is a left S-module, so left Noetherianity is the relevant finiteness side.
Restriction maps over reverse-inclusion neighbourhoods form the required direct systems and are compatible with one fixed free resolution and the open-restriction-compatible Godement construction.
Exact filtered colimits pass through page homology, finite direct sums, and the finite abutment filtrations.
First-quadrant stabilization is uniform in each bidegree and total degree.
The filtered colimit of neighbourhood Ext groups identifies with the stalk of the sheafified Ext presheaf.
The componentwise Ext-colimit comparison hypotheses give the stated comparison and collapse results.
The quotient/change-of-rings E2 indexing and finite direct sums are correct.
Left Noetherianity supplies degreewise finite-free resolutions for the finitely generated Tor_a^R(S,M), so the required Ext functors commute with filtered colimits.
The candidate uses the admitted repaired Tor_a^R(S,M) everywhere.

planned_mapping.aggregation: Existing p.191--192 constant-sheaf Ext lemmas plus D1011 cover the remaining substantive section children; HLC and failure illustrations remain nonblocking example_or_remark units.

nonclaims: D1011 does not formalize the p.193 HLC example or the subsequent failure example; those are nonblocking example_or_remark units.
D1011 makes no analytic-geometry, coherent-sheaf, or equivariant-vector-bundle claim.
Functoriality of the quotient hyper-Ext system is claimed from the E2 page onward, not from an unconstructed E1 page.
No unconditional Ext/filtered-colimit interchange is claimed; the general comparison lemma states the required componentwise hypotheses explicitly.
The Noetherian specialization uses left Noetherianity and finitely generated left S-modules; it does not assert right Noetherianity.
No new source correction is made; the admitted p.193 Tor-base repair is inherited exactly.
This design audit does not edit live cohomology.tex, build a PDF, mutate a semantic or mapping ledger, or perform a Git/GitHub/publication action.
